answer_summary: P6 is a six-porphyrin nanobelt with two butadiyne bridges per meso-meso junction. Along the continuous global pi pathway each porphyrin unit contributes 7 double-bond equivalents (3 porphyrin-rim C=C plus 2 used doubles from each of the 2 butadiyne bridges), i.e. 14 pi electrons, so neutral P6 has 6 x 14 = 84 = 4 x 21 pi electrons (globally anti-aromatic, matching the problem statement). The first Hueckel 4k+2 count reached by oxidation is 82 = 4 x 20 + 2, so the minimum number of electrons to remove is n(e) = 2 and the global aromatic system holds n(t) = 82 pi electrons.
assumptions: Hueckel's rule (4k+2 aromatic / 4k anti-aromatic for a closed cyclic conjugated pi system) is the trusted general law the question explicitly invokes.
